messages.subject: Stacked Bar Charts
parts:
Hello,

I have the following data set:

theta treet vist pusht
0.025 0.213899 219.208000 0.054594
0.050 0.213610 92.347300 0.052089
0.075 0.224615 46.297900 0.053300
0.100 0.219075 24.887200 0.053001
0.125 0.214350 17.958100 0.053904

Where theta is a tree parameter and treet, vist and pusht are
(measured) times. I wish to produce a stacked bar chart with the
value of theta along the x-avis and treet+vist+pusht (the total time)
as the bar height. I can do this as:

qplot(factor(theta), vist+pusht+treet,data=d, geom = "bar")

But what I can not figure out is how to fill the bars based off of the
contributions of treet, vist and pusht. I have tried
fill=c(treet,vist,pusht) to no avail but I really am not sure how to
approach the problem. (I know I've picked a rather bad piece of data
with vist dominating -- however in general all three times are of the
same magnitude).

Regards, Freddie.

Freddie
This is my first response to the group. I suggest that you try the following 

fred <- read.csv("theta.csv") # read the file

meltfred <- melt(fred, id.vars = "theta") # melt by theta 

qplot(factor(theta), value, data=meltfred, geom="bar", fill=variable) # proportional bars only by visit

I am not sure why the other categories do not show. Maybe the distribution of data?

Someone will suggest something better

messages.subject: Re: Stacked Bar Charts
parts:
library("reshape") # for melt
library("ggplot2")

dd<-melt(d,id='theta') #'wide' format to 'long' format
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=dd, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")

How about as above?
# This 'wide' / 'long' format issue is one of troubles for beginners
such as I.
# e.g.
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/c0ec4b776b28a051/beacc26e4545e0f0?lnk=gst&q=Stacked+Bar+Charts#beacc26e4545e0f0

# Tips
# 1. How to use only a part of variables.
# 1-1. melt with given column names only.
# (use given names during 'wide' to 'long').
d2<-d
d2$vist_per100<-d2$vist/100
d2$pusht_m0_05_x1000<-(d2$pusht - 0.05)*1000
d2$treet_m0_21_x100<-(d2$treet - 0.21)*100

d3<-melt(d2,id='theta',
measure.vars=c('treet_m0_21_x100','vist_per100','pusht_m0_05_x1000'))
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=d3, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")

# 1-2. choose rows of given variables and drop unused levels.
# (use given names when already 'wide')
dd<-melt(d,id='theta')
d4<-dd[dd[,'variable'] %in% c('vist','pusht'),] # choose rows of given
variables
d4[,'variable']<-d4[,'variable'][,drop=TRUE] # drop unused levels
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=d4, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")

# 2. reorder variables.
d3<-melt(d2,id='theta',
measure.vars=c('treet_m0_21_x100','vist_per100','pusht_m0_05_x1000'))
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=d3, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")
d3[,2]<-factor(d3[,
2],c('pusht_m0_05_x1000','vist_per100','treet_m0_21_x100')) #reorder
variables
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=d3, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")

# 3. change order of legend separately from plot.
# from
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/a1eb9d1a57de9ba7/10c682b40a3b865f?lnk=gst&q=coord_flip+legend#10c682b40a3b865f
vars<-c('treet_m0_21_x100','vist_per100','pusht_m0_05_x1000')
d3<-melt(d2,id='theta', measure.vars=vars)
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=d3, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")
qplot(factor(theta), value, data=d3, fill=factor(variable), geom =
"bar")+scale_fill_hue(breaks=rev(vars))
